title: Compute shaders with `buffer_get_data_async` not working
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4.1 stable

### System information

PopOS! 22.04, NVidia GTX 1070, Vulkan, driver 470.256.02

### Issue description

I am trying to run a compute shader and get the result from the GPU asynchronously to reduce freezes. For this I figured there is a `RenderingDevice.buffer_get_data_async` method, which I would like to use. I tried to make it work but couldn't get this method to retrieve the correct data. It seems to always retrieve the initial data I used for the buffer.  I am not sure if the issue I have is due to a bug or a misunderstanding / misuse of the `buffer_get_data_async` method.

### Steps to reproduce

With gdscript:
- Use local rendering device
- Run compute shader that fills a buffer
- Get a buffer content with `buffer_get_data_async`
- The buffer content is the one that was set before running the compute shader

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I have setup a small reproduction project here : https://github.com/AntoineRR/godot-compute-shader-experiment

In this project I get the data with `buffer_get_data` or `buffer_get_data_async` depending on the button pressed. The buffer retrieved is expected to contain elements that are equal to their index in the array (this is the code in the `test.glsl` file). It works with the sync version but the buffer is filled with zeros in the async version.
